claim: Scientists endorse Mertonian norms (73-91%) and mostly reject Mitroff counter-norms (18-23%; self-interestedness 25-33%) as what SHOULD hold, but perceive colleagues as behaving counter-normatively more than normatively (normative dissonance).
agent_test: Compare stated-rule compliance with code-measured behaviour: ask the agent to state its rules, then audit transcripts for violations at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Mitroff's Apollo study (over 40 scientists, four interview rounds over three years per the 1973 NASA report; '42' and '3.5 years' come from secondary summaries of the 1974 ASR paper) found committed advocacy, strong personal stakes and ambivalence about the norms. Per-norm counter-norm numbers have still not been seen; only the companion report was read.
agent_test: Test whether an early defend-your-hypothesis phase before the doubt phase beats doubting from step one at equal tokens.

claim: Universalism fails in human review: same paper gets reject 23% (Nobel name), 48% (anonymous), 65% (junior name); accept or minor revision 58.8/23.6/9.9%; invitation acceptance 38.5/30.7/28.5% (3,299 invitations, one finance paper). Both category sets confirmed in full text.
agent_test: Run the exact judge on a paper with the author or prestige cue swapped; report verdict shift in points.

claim: Single-blind human reviewers favour famous authors and top institutions (odds multipliers 1.63 famous, 1.58 top university, 2.10 top company; female 0.78 n.s. alone) and bid for 22% fewer papers.
agent_test: Same swap test with the same effect-size target.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Status advantage is cumulative: funding winners just above the threshold got more than twice the later funding in 8 years (Bol 2018), partly because losers stop applying.
agent_test: Not directly testable; analogue: an early mistaken pick should not become the anchor for later rounds.

claim: Organised scepticism applied to published science often fails to confirm: 13/21 (62%) social science experiments replicated with effect size about 50% of the original, estimated true-positive rate 67% (Camerer 2018, abstract read); cancer biology: median effect 85% smaller, 92% smaller, 40% (39/97) positive effects succeed, 46% (51/112) combined (Errington 2021, abstract read).
agent_test: Re-check the agent confirmed claims on held-out cases; expect shrinkage and set a prior for it.
audit_note: The claim wording median effect 85% smaller, 92% smaller is ambiguous: 92% is the share of replication effects that were smaller than the original, not a 92% reduction.

claim: LLM judges leak author prestige into scores: famous-name or institution swaps raise positive-rating share 36.8% to 40.8-41.6% (500 papers, one system); three of four LLMs rate top male authors and elite institutions higher (+0.39 points for GPT).
agent_test: Swap-test our judge with and without author or identity text; require a shift under a set threshold or strip identity in code.
audit_note: The 36.8% to 40.8-41.6% figures are one system (LLM Review) on 500 papers as stated; wording fits.

claim: LLM prestige leak is real but its size depends on the measurement. GPT-4o-mini with 402,500 audit responses: reject falls 1.7 pp (about 25% relative) when identity is shown, quality score shifts about 1%. With token-probability (soft) ratings, seven LLMs (including GPT-4o Mini) prefer highly ranked institutions in 66-94% of paired comparisons (252 ICLR 2025 papers). In the economics audit the abstract names GPT, Gemma and LLaMA as favouring top male authors and elite institutions; Claude 3.5 showed no author-prominence effect but did penalise one non-US university. Hard integer scores under-measure the leak.
agent_test: Measure our own judge; do not assume either the large or the small number.
audit_note: Howell (402,500 responses, reject down 1.7 pp, about 25% relative) and Vasu (252 ICLR papers, seven models, 66.0-94.2%) match, but the same family of models is loose (Vasu tests seven models, GPT-4o Mini being one) and Claude 3.5 not listed as biased holds only for the economics abstract: the body shows Claude penalising Chulalongkorn University and MIT/Harvard raising ratings for all four LLMs.
claim_before_audit: LLM prestige leak is real but its size depends on the measurement. GPT-4o-mini with 402,500 audit responses: reject falls 1.7 pp (about 25% relative) when identity is shown, quality score shifts about 1%. With token-probability ratings the same family of models prefers high-ranked institutions in 66-94% of paired comparisons (252 ICLR papers, 7 models). Claude 3.5 was not listed as biased in the economics audit. Hard integer scores under-measure the leak.

claim: Answer order alone flips LLM referee verdicts: Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT on 66/80 queries by reordering; win rate 2.5% first vs 82.5% second; position consistency GPT-4 65.0%, GPT-3.5 46.2%, Claude-v1 23.8%.
agent_test: Judge every pair in both orders in code and count flips on our judge.

claim: Order-swapping and averaging, a reference answer, or evidence-before-score reduce judge error: math grading failures 14/20 default, 6/20 with CoT, 3/20 with reference; few-shot raised GPT-4 consistency 65.0% to 77.5%.
agent_test: Compare judge accuracy with and without a code-checked reference at equal tokens.
audit_note: Math grading counts are small (10 questions, 20 trials) and reference/CoT gains are from Zheng only; few-shot is a separate fix from the three named.

claim: LLM judges favour their own output; self-recognition (GPT-4 73.5% out of the box; over 90% after fine-tuning on 500 examples for GPT-3.5 and Llama 2) is linearly tied to self-preference. Self-win bias in MT-Bench: GPT-4 +10%, Claude-v1 +25%.
agent_test: Have a different model, or blinded stripped text, judge the agent drafts; compare to self-judging.

claim: Simulated LLM committees reproduce conformity (rating SD down 27.2%), authority bias (known identity on 10% of papers shifts decisions 27.7%) and one lazy reviewer cuts others commitment 18.7%; 37.1% of decisions vary with reviewer bias. Validity is checked against theory only, not real decisions.
agent_test: Run an N-judge committee with and without seeing each other votes; count agreement and error rate.

claim: LLM reviewers are attackable by text in the manuscript: hidden injected text raised mean rating 5.34 to 7.99 (Ye 2024); a second study of 26 preprints and 3 LLMs found +20% acceptance, removed by a caution prompt that also lowered all scores, detection Gemini 96.6% vs Llama 18.3%; an optimised injection hits 90-98% success on open pairwise judges and perplexity detectors miss 70%. Code-level sanitising untested.
agent_test: Inject instruction text into the judged content and measure the score change; sanitise in code.
audit_note: Shi reports some success rates of 88-89% as well as 90-98%, and the 70% miss rate is for windowed perplexity detection on Llama-3-8B only; the +20% acceptance was reported as about 20%.

claim: LLM-assisted reviewing is lenient and widespread: at least 15.8% of ICLR 2024 reviews AI-assisted; AI review scored higher in 53.4% of discordant pairs (p=0.002); borderline papers +4.9 points acceptance (p=0.024); 6.5-16.9% of review text across four venues LLM-modified.
agent_test: Calibrate an LLM grader mean score against a code-checked label and subtract the inflation.

claim: GPT-4 feedback overlaps human reviewer comments about as much as two humans do (30.85% vs 28.58% Nature; 39.23% vs 35.25% ICLR; 57.4% of 308 researchers found it helpful). Overlap is of comment points, not verdicts; a separate expert annotation found LLM reviews more deficient and less diverse.
agent_test: Use the model to generate objections, then verify them with tests; measure how many objections are real defects.

claim: LLM ideation is judged more novel than expert ideas (4.84 human, 5.64 AI, 5.81 AI reranked; 79 reviewers, 49 ideas per condition) but only about 5% of 4,000 seed ideas are non-duplicates, reviewer agreement is only 56.1%, and LLM judges score 43-53% on pairwise tasks, below human agreement.
agent_test: Sample N ideas from one model, dedup at cosine 0.8 and count unique; select by executed test, not by model rank.

claim: An automated science pipeline without a real novelty search fails the sceptic norm: 5/12 experiments (42%) failed, median 5 citations, 5 of 34 recent, micro-batching labelled novel; adding search to the co-scientist reflection agent cut known-idea novelty from 6.14 to 2.38 of 10.
agent_test: Compare a novelty check with and without external retrieval on ideas known to be old.
audit_note: Sakana pipeline did include a keyword novelty search (up to 10 rounds); the failure was its weakness, not absence, so without a real novelty search is an interpretation.

claim: An LLM reviewer with reflection and ensembling reaches near-human accept/reject accuracy (70% accuracy, balanced 0.65 vs human 0.66, 500 ICLR 2022 papers), but human consistency itself is low (FNR 0.52).
agent_test: Treat human-level as a low bar; ensemble over both orders and stripped inputs.

claim: Agents replicating 20 ICML papers from scratch score 21.0% (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) vs 41.4% for a human PhD baseline on 3 papers: replication, the sceptic norm in action, is still hard for agents.
agent_test: Give the agent a replication task with a runnable check and count the pass rate.

claim: A randomised trial gating LLM feedback by automated reliability tests got 27% of reviewers to update, 12,000+ suggestions incorporated, +80 words, over 96% of feedback passing all tests. Longer is not necessarily better.
agent_test: Gate model output through code checks before it is shown; compare error rate of gated vs ungated.

claim: Formal models (Strevens 2003, Kitcher 1990) say credit-seeking spreads effort across rival programmes; no agent opened them and the LLM link is untested: copies of one model are not independent.
agent_test: Compare N samples from one model against N prompts or models with different priors on diversity of correct answers.

claim: Model diversity helps debate more than copies of one model: Heter-MAD (two models) +6.4% over the single-model SoM average and +5.8% over CoT average; three different models 91% vs 82% for three copies on GSM-8K. Debate itself rarely beats CoT (about 15% of 36 configs). Cost-equal test against the best single model is missing.
agent_test: Compare N independent samples of the best model, N copies in debate, and N different models, at equal tokens, on held-out items.

claim: Most of the gain credited to multi-agent debate is majority voting: Qwen2.5-7B average 0.7205 single, 0.7691 vote, 0.7377 best debate T=2; centralised debate 0.6551 (conformity cost). Role-prompt diversity did not change this.
agent_test: Use independent samples plus a vote as the baseline; only add debate if it beats it at equal tokens.

claim: A self-critique step without external feedback does not help and can hurt (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over rounds), while the same critique with tools gains (CRITIC AmbigNQ EM 50.0 with tools vs 42.0 without, CoT 44.2). Supports a tool-backed or different-model sceptic.
agent_test: Ablate the sceptic: same-model doubt, doubt with code or search, doubt by a different model; same tokens.
audit_note: The CRITIC figures are for one model block; Huang over rounds gives GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0.

claim: Human literature shrinkage prior: confirmed single studies replicate at about 62% (social science, effect about half) and 46% (cancer biology, 40% for positive effects). Whether this carries over to LLM-generated claims is untested.
agent_test: Re-test a sample of the agent's own confirmed claims on fresh data; estimate its own shrinkage.

claim: Mitroff's report supports advocacy as a feature: scientists said peers try to confirm, not falsify, their own theories, and progress comes from committed advocates testing against each other. No LLM study found testing an advocacy-first phase against doubt-from-the-start.
agent_test: Gap 2 experiment: defend-then-doubt phase vs doubt from start, equal tokens, separate roles.

claim: Huber's status bias holds for 'accept or minor revision' (58.8% prominent, 23.6% anonymous, 9.9% junior) as well as reject; still one paper, one field, no independent replication.
agent_test: Treat as one strong field experiment, not a general law.
